title: Targeting Key Factors to Realizing Improved Global Vaccination Coverage
text:
Vaccination coverage rates are affected by multiple and varied societal and personal factors​. To better understand these factors at a global scale, the University of Washington Population Health Initiative led an interdisciplinary research team that undertook a study that ended in February 2023 to better understand how countries can realistically improve vaccination coverage, and how such improvement will affect the overall burden of vaccine-preventable diseases in that country.


Related Publication: (Rios Casas et al. 2024)

title: Local health data analysis and communication toolkit
text:
Analysts at local health departments, especially those working with small numbers, face many common challenges that can affect how confidently and clearly they can answer questions from leadership, community members, and the media. A group of analysts and communications professionals in Washington State, mostly working at local health jurisdictions, have produced progressive editions of the Local Health Data Analysis and Communication Toolkit to support analysts in this work.
Personal Role: Led the creation of a new “Coding in R section” and served as a general contributor.
Local health data analysis and communication toolkit, 3rd edition. (December 22, 2025, update). Available online.

title: WA Mortality Record Harmonization
text: WA Local Health Departments are provided death certificate data by the WA DOH Center for Health Statistics (CHS), but the format of these data files has changed across years and data systems making historical analysis difficult. This project created an ETL system to create a harmonized multi-year mortality file which can be used for in-depth population health analysis from 2010 - present. This project was completed with select members of the Washington State LHJ Analytic Resources Group.
